verses.text: Saul was still threatening the Lord’s disciples with violence and death. He went to the high priest
and asked for letters to the synagogues in Damascus. He wanted permission to arrest anyone he found following the Way, men or women, and bring them bound to Jerusalem.
As he traveled and neared Damascus, a light from heaven suddenly flashed around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice say, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?”
He asked, “Who are you, Lord?” The Lord said, “I am Jesus, the one you are persecuting.
“Now get up and go into the city. There you’ll be told what you must do.”
The men traveling with him stood there speechless. They heard the voice but saw no one.
Saul got up from the ground. When he opened his eyes, he couldn’t see anything, so they led him by the hand into Damascus.
For three days he couldn’t see, and he neither ate nor drank.
There was a disciple in Damascus named Ananias. The Lord called to him in a vision, “Ananias!” He answered, “Here I am, Lord.”
The Lord told him, “Get up and go to the street called Straight. At the house of Judas, ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul. He is praying right now.
“In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come in and lay hands on him so that he can see again.”
Ananias replied, “Lord, I’ve heard from many people about all the harm this man has done to your holy people in Jerusalem.
“He has authority from the chief priests here to arrest everyone who calls on your name.”
But the Lord told him, “Go. I have chosen him to carry my name before the nations, their kings, and the people of Israel.
“I will show him how much he must suffer for my name.”
Ananias went to the house and laid his hands on Saul. He said, “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road here, sent me so you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
At once something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptized.
He ate and regained his strength. Saul stayed several days with the disciples in Damascus.
Right away he began preaching in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.
Everyone who heard him was amazed. They said, “Isn’t this the man who attacked those in Jerusalem who call on this name? Didn’t he come here to arrest them and take them to the chief priests?”
But Saul grew stronger and left the Jews living in Damascus confused, proving that Jesus is the Messiah.
After many days, the Jews plotted together to kill him.
Saul learned about their plan. They watched the city gates day and night, hoping to kill him.
But his disciples took him by night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the city wall.
When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him and didn’t believe he was a disciple.
Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and explained how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, how the Lord had spoken to him, and how Saul had boldly preached in Jesus’ name in Damascus.
So Saul stayed with them and moved freely around Jerusalem,
speaking boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus. He argued with the Greek-speaking Jews, who then tried to kill him.
When the believers found out, they took him to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
Then the churches throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and grew stronger. They lived in reverence for the Lord and in the Holy Spirit’s comfort, and their numbers increased.
As Peter traveled through the region, he also visited the holy people living in Lydda.
There he met a man named Aeneas, who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.
Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed.” At once he got up.
Everyone living in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha, which means Dorcas. She was always doing good and helping people in need.
Around that time she became sick and died. They washed her body and laid her in an upstairs room.
Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard Peter was there. They sent two men to him, urging him, “Please come to us right away.”
Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they took him upstairs. All the widows stood around him crying and showing him the tunics and other clothes Dorcas had made while she was with them.
Peter sent everyone out, knelt down, and prayed. Then he turned toward the body and said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, saw Peter, and sat up.
He gave her his hand and helped her stand. Then he called the holy people and the widows and presented her alive.
News of this spread throughout Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.
Peter stayed in Joppa for many days with a tanner named Simon.
